claims.claim: Climate change impacts such as intense droughts, dust exposure, regular air-quality emergencies from fires, and ozone concentrations will make unhealthy outdoor air a regular condition in many cities, potentially rendering some places uninhabitable.
claims.supporting_excerpt: droughts will intensify dust exposure; fires will regularly produce air-quality emergencies, and increasing ozone concentrations as well as altered weather patterns will make unhealthy outdoor air a regular condition of life in an increasing number of cities. At an extreme, these developments may make some places simply uninhabitable, as much as if they had been submerged.

claims.claim: The first type of artificial adaptation, the carapace, consists of protective equipment and material designed to insulate human bodies from an increasingly hostile atmosphere, aligning with neoliberal tendencies to convert public problems into individual challenges.
claims.supporting_excerpt: I call this the "carapace," using the term broadly to refer to a wide range of protective equipment and material designed to insulate human bodies from an increasingly hostile atmosphere. The evocation of a hard shell is intentional, and is meant to resonate with midcentury images of modern human bodies as hybrids of flesh and steel to which Arendt occasionally referred

definitions.definition: A wide range of protective equipment and material designed to insulate human bodies from an increasingly hostile atmosphere.

must_not_be_lost: The connection between the carapace and midcentury images of human bodies as hybrids of flesh and steel.
output.segment_function: Discussing climate change conditions that make outdoor air unhealthy and introducing the first type of artificial adaptation, the carapace, based on philosophical reflection.
unresolved_context: Discussion of interlocking inequalities of wealth, health, power, and regard referenced to be continued at the end of the article.
Two additional types of adaptation besides the carapace.
